extracted.intended_audience: LEA and IHE administrators, Title IX coordinators, institutional legal counsel, compliance officers, and policy stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory Impact Analysis and implementation assumptions for the Department of Education's final Title IX regulations, covering baseline estimates, cost and time burdens, required procedures, recordkeeping, and alternatives considered for LEAs, IHEs, and other recipients of federal education funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Clery data multiplier to estimate IHE baseline investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Clery Act data as a proxy to transform limited Senate subcommittee data into an estimate of total investigations; apply a multiplier of 1.416 to account for inclusion of dating violence, domestic violence, and stalking, yielding an assumed baseline of 5.70 investigations per year per IHE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge weaknesses of Clery data (may not capture all sexual harassment incidents) but treat it as best available proxy; the Department requested alternatives but received none of sufficient quality. Use positive correlation between Clery reports and underlying incidents when applying multiplier.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEA baseline investigations from CRDC
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume LEAs currently conduct approximately 3.23 Title IX investigations each year based on Civil Rights Data Collection (CRDC) school-year 2015-2016 reporting of harassment incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department lacks direct info on number of LEA investigations; uses CRDC incidents as the basis for baseline and then applies additional assumptions (e.g., that only 50% of such incidents would result in a formal complaint under final regs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient grouping for cost-effect estimates (three-group model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume recipients fall into one of three groups: (1) compliant with statutory/regulatory requirements and not operating at 2011 DCL/2014 Q&A levels; (2) continued activity at 2011 DCL/2014 Q&A levels but will amend to levels required under current statute and proposed regs (most likely to experience net cost savings); (3) continued 2011 DCL/2014 Q&A-level activity and will continue to do so after final regs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use estimated shares to model impacts: assume 5% of LEAs and IHEs in Group 1; 90% of LEAs in Group 2 and 5% in Group 3; for IHEs assume 50% experience any cost savings (Group 2) and 45% in Group 3. For 'other entities' assume 90% in Group 1 and 5% in each other group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumed personnel wage rates and employer cost factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Use median hourly wages for education sector personnel from BLS and apply an employer cost for employee compensation rate of 1.46 when monetizing hourly burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply loaded wage rates to all time estimates; specific loaded rates cited (e.g., Title IX Coordinator loaded rate $65.22/hr for educational administrators, attorney $90.71/hr) and used consistently across cost calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to read and understand final regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume recipients will need time to review and understand final regulations: LEA — 4 hours for Title IX Coordinator and 8 hours for an attorney; IHE — 8 hours for Title IX Coordinator and 16 hours for an attorney; other entities — 4 hours Coordinator and 8 hours attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These were retained from the NPRM except where corrected; estimate monetized cost of this activity (~$30,324,610). Include any corrected omissions from NPRM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to revise grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume recipients must revise grievance procedures with these time estimates: LEA — 6 hours Title IX Coordinator, 24 hours attorney, plus 2 hours administrator review; IHE — 12 hours Title IX Coordinator, 28 hours attorney, plus 4 hours administrator review; other entities — 4/16/2 hours respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates were revised in response to public comment and are used to compute costs (~$82,441,460). Recipients should create or modify forms/procedures consistent with §106.45 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting non-discrimination statement burden and coverage assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume 40% of LEAs, 20% of IHEs, and 100% of other entities will need to post their non-discrimination statement; time estimates per recipient role: LEA — 0.5 hr each for Title IX Coordinator and attorney, plus 2 hrs for web developer; IHE — 1 hr each for Coordinator and attorney, plus 2 hrs web developer; other entities similar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use web developer hourly rate cited ($44.12/hr) in monetization. These percentages and hours were not revised from the NPRM absent public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements and assumed durations
rubrics_metrics.description: Require recipients to train Title IX Coordinators, an investigator, any person designated to facilitate informal resolution, and two decision-makers (assuming an additional decision-maker for appeals). Training assumed to take ~8 hours for staff at LEA and IHE levels; other entities assumed 4 hours for the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training cost estimates revised since NPRM in response to public comment; Year 1 and recurring-year costs estimated (~$52,135,230 Year 1; $26,067,620 each subsequent year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation requirement contingent on formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations require recipients to conduct an investigation only if a formal complaint of sexual harassment is filed by the complainant or signed by the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy change is expected to reduce number of investigations. Use Clery Act correlations and institutional-size gap-closing assumptions (assumed 40% reduction in gap between large and small IHEs) to estimate reductions in investigations (per-IHE reduction of 1.60 from formal-complaint gating and 0.29 from limiting to education program/activity contexts, total ~1.89 reduction for Group 2 IHEs). For LEAs, assume 50% of CRDC incidents would result in a formal complaint, yielding a 1.62 reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures obligations and cost assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(a) requires Title IX Coordinators to promptly contact complainants, discuss availability of supportive measures, consider complainant's wishes, inform about availability with or without formal complaint, and explain process for filing a formal complaint. Supportive measures must be offered without fee or charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department adds a flat cost assumption of $250 per set of supportive measures provided and includes time burdens for students. Time estimates per informal response: LEA — 3 hrs Title IX Coordinator, 8 hrs administrative assistant, and 12 hrs each for two students (K-12 minimum wage); IHE — 3 hrs Coordinator, 16 hrs admin, 24 hrs each for two students; other entities average K-12 and postsecondary student rates. Monetized cost estimated at ~$31,164,490/year. The Department does not estimate costs for particular supportive measures beyond the flat fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time/cost for jurisdictional determination (education program or activity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize instances where recipients will expend time/resources to determine if an incident occurred within the recipient's education program or activity or otherwise would require investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume ~4 hours for a Title IX Coordinator and 12 hours for an investigator at LEA and IHE levels; assume negligible occurrence at other entities. Monetized estimate of this activity is ~$10,338,310/year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal investigation time and per-hearing nominal cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumed staff-time per formal investigation: LEA — 8 hrs Title IX Coordinator, 16 hrs administrative assistant, 8 hrs each for two advisors (attorney wage rate), 20 hrs investigator, 8 hrs decision-maker, 12 hrs each for two students. IHE — 24 hrs Title IX Coordinator, 40 hrs administrative assistant, 60 hrs each for two advisors, 40 hrs investigator, 16 hrs decision-maker, 24 hrs each for two students. Other entities approximate LEA levels. Add a nominal $100 cost per hearing for recordkeeping/technology (e.g., video conferencing for cross-examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions from public comment included increasing attorney/advisor time, including students in time accounting, adding the $100 per-hearing nominal charge, and updating counts of formal investigations. Use these to compute net reductions/increases in burden (e.g., reduction associated with fewer investigations estimated ~$189,134,990/year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance cost increases for recipients not currently compliant
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume some recipients are not currently conducting investigations in a manner compliant with final regs and will incur increased time costs: LEA — additional 2 hrs Title IX Coordinator, 3 hrs administrative assistant, 8 hrs each for two advisors, 10 hrs investigator, 8 hrs decision-maker. IHE — additional 6 hrs Title IX Coordinator, 10 hrs administrative assistant, 60 hrs each for two advisors, 20 hrs investigator, 16 hrs decision-maker. Other entities — 2/4/1/10/4 hrs respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include nominal additional charge for recordkeeping/technology for all entities. Monetized increase for analytical Group 1 estimated ~$21,867,410/year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals assumptions and time estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume 50% of all decisions result in appeal. Time per appeal: LEA — 4 hrs Title IX Coordinator, 8 hrs administrative assistant, 8 hrs each for two advisors, 8 hrs decision-maker, 12 hrs each for two students. IHE — ~12 hrs Title IX Coordinator, 20 hrs administrative assistant, 16 hrs each for two advisors, 8 hrs decision-maker, 24 hrs each for two students. Other entities mirror LEA assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised from NPRM to increase advisor and student time contributions. Monetized total cost estimated at ~$62,024,720/year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution assumptions and net effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume 25% of formal complaints will be resolved through an informal resolution process. When used, informal resolution reduces investigator and advisor time by half, eliminates time for decision-makers and hearing-related recordkeeping/technology costs, but increases time for administrative assistants and the person designated to facilitate informal resolution (not the Title IX Coordinator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume facilitator is a person designated by the recipient other than the Title IX Coordinator. Increased admin/facilitator time: LEA/other entities add 4 hrs admin + 4 hrs facilitator; IHE add 8 hrs admin + 8 hrs facilitator. Net annual cost savings estimated at ~$29,694,690.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and documentation setup and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Require recipients to maintain specified documentation about Title IX activities with higher first-year setup costs and lower maintenance out-year costs. Time estimates: LEA Year 1 — 4 hrs Title IX Coordinator + 8 hrs administrative assistant; IHE Year 1 — 24 hrs Title IX Coordinator, 40 hrs administrative assistant, 40 hrs database administrator (at $50.71/hr). Out-years: LEA — 2 hrs Coordinator + 4 hrs admin; IHE — 4 hrs Coordinator, 40 hrs admin, 8 hrs DBA. Other entities assumed to face LEA-like burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetized recordkeeping/documentation cost estimated ~$39,114,530 in Year 1 and ~$15,189,260 in each subsequent year. Recipients are assumed to likely use electronic databases (especially IHEs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory alternatives evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider three main alternatives: (1) leave current regulations/guidance unchanged; (2) leave current regs and reinstate 2011 Dear Colleague Letter or 2014 Q&A; (3) issue regulations that add broad statements of general principles for recipients' grievance procedures. Rejected alternatives because they would (inter alia) be legally inadequate or too vague.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department rejected (2) for reasons stated in the NPRM (procedural/substantive problems with 2011 DCL/2014 Q&A) and (1) because current regs are silent on whether Title IX covers sexual harassment — leaving protections only to non-binding guidance. Rejected (3) because vagueness would not provide predictability or consistency across recipients. Chosen criteria for preferred option included clarity, legally binding standards, predictability, fairness, and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting statement cost/benefit categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify monetized annual costs, benefits, and transfers into categories (e.g., reading/understanding the rule; revision of grievance procedures; posting non-discrimination statement; training; response to informal reports; reduction in number of investigations; increased investigation requirements; appeals; informal resolution; creation and maintenance of documentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List monetized values in the Accounting Statement table and note some benefits (clarity, fairness, preservation of constitutional rights) are 'Not Quantified.' Use this classification when presenting net cost over ten years (~$48.6 to $62.2 million).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act small-entity definitions and impact threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'small' entities for impact assessment: 'small' IHE — two-year IHE with enrollment <500 FTE or four-year IHE with enrollment <1,000 FTE; 'small' LEA — annual revenues < $7,000,000; small entity counts estimated (~631 small IHEs and ~7,900 small LEAs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions and average revenues to compute percent-of-revenue burdens: small IHE estimated burden ~$28,065/year (~0.28% of avg revenue $9,925,999); small LEA estimated burden ~$11,978/year (~0.26% of avg revenue $4,565,342). Department certifies no significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act burden estimates for specific information collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide burden estimates for specific record/notice/information-collection items: §106.44(b)(3) removed (no burden); §106.45(b)(2) Written Notice of Allegations — create/modify form: 1 hr Title IX Coordinator + 0.5 hr attorney (Year 1 cost $2,650,654; total burden 35,958 hours over retention); §106.45(b)(9) Informal Resolution — same per-recipient form burden and same aggregate burden and costs. Record retention period considered (three-year calculation and seven-year retention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate forms are created once and maintenance burden captured under recordkeeping. Even if not all recipients offer informal resolution, burden is estimated for 100% of recipients to be conservative. Use OMB Control Number 1870-NEW and recordkeeping retention periods when reporting aggregate hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on informal resolution for employee-on-student allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients that offer informal resolution may not offer or facilitate an informal resolution process to resolve allegations that an employee sexually harassed a student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit procedural limitation embedded in §106.45(b)(9) and must be implemented in policy/forms.
